images.section_title: Introduction to Delaying a Signal
images.image_description: Two-panel instructional signal graph on a clean Cartesian grid. Left panel shows a simple continuous-time signal $x(t)$ with one clear peak at $t_0$, visible support boundaries, and labeled time-axis markers. Right panel shows $y(t)=x(t-T)$ on the same scale, with the entire waveform shifted right by $T$ so the peak moves from $t_0$ to $t_0+T$ and the support moves from $[a,b]$ to $[a+T,b+T]$. Include a clear rightward arrow labeled $T$ between corresponding feature markers. No decorative elements.
images.report: Two-panel tent comparison with labeled support boundaries and peak times.; Single figure-level shift arrow between corresponding peaks.
images.lesson_core_move: Delay a continuous-time signal by shifting each key time point, breakpoint, and support interval T units to the right while preserving the signal's shape and values.
